### Through the Valley to the Victory
Author: Carolyn Dale Newell
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement-cafe/through-the-valley-to-the-victory-encouragement-caf-july-22-2019.html
Passage: Joshua 8:1
Points:
- Unplanned trials and battles are an inescapable part of the Christian walk.
- Joshua walked directly into a dark valley, trusting the battle plan God provided.
- Fear tempts believers to retreat when facing overwhelming and painful circumstances.
- God fights behind the scenes and ambushes the enemy when we feel trapped.
- Enduring the valley under God's guidance leads believers straight into His promised victory.

### The Spiritual Fight Against Fear
Author: Daily Disciples Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-disciples/daily-disciples-may-18.html
Passage: Joshua 8:1
Points:
- Previous defeat and the consequences of sin can leave believers immobilized by fear.
- God commanded Joshua to rise, return to Ai, and finish the assignment.
- God's instruction to see requires spiritual eyes of faith before victory is visible.
- Discouragement and past failure must not keep believers from moving forward.
- Trusting the Lord's faithfulness enables believers to take the next obedient step.

### Spoiled by the Grace of God
Author: Tyler Kenney
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/spoiled-by-the-grace-of-god
Passage: Joshua 8:1-2
Points:
- Israel's painful defeat at Ai traced back to Achan's covetous theft at Jericho.
- Human thinking assumes God would impose stricter limits following Israel's disobedience.
- After Israel repented, God responded by displaying even greater generosity and grace.
- God granted Israel the spoils of Ai—the very blessing sin sought illicitly.
- Repentant believers are met not with harsh withholding, but with God's abundant mercy.

### Are You Afraid or Discouraged?
Author: Gwen Smith
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/girlfriends-in-god-july-4-2019.html
Passage: Joshua 8:1
Points:
- Stepping into major responsibilities naturally provokes feelings of anxiety and fear.
- God continually anchored Joshua with reminders not to be afraid or dismayed.
- The Lord never expects believers to handle challenging tasks using only their own strength.
- Faithfulness in small duties prepares individuals to follow God into new adventures.
- Believers can step out boldly because God Himself serves as their guide and defender.
